speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent bleeding after a wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; to begin our investigation, have you experienced any spontaneous bleeding or bleeding that lasted longer than usual in other situations, such as after shaving or a minor cut?

REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time (PT)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hematocrit: 35%, Leukocyte_Count: 8,500/mm3, Platelet_Count: 160,000/mm3, Prothrombin_Time: 15 sec, Activated_Partial_Thromboplastin_Time: 60 sec

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, joint pains (except noted in family history), or significant past illnesses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That previous diagnosis of gastroenteritis does not explain your bleeding symptoms; can you describe the specific appearance and location of your bruises, and do they appear spontaneously without any injury? REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Function_Assay
REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_Bruise_Photograph

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PLATELET FUNCTION ASSAY: PROLONGED BLEEDING TIME SKIN BRUISE PHOTOGRAPH: MULTIPLE ECCHYMOTIC LESIONS OF VARYING AGES NOTED ON EXTREMITIES

speaker: Doctor
text: The platelet function assay shows a prolonged bleeding time, and your photographs reveal multiple ecchymotic lesions of varying ages on your extremities; these findings strongly suggest a qualitative platelet defect or von Willebrand disease rather than a coagulation factor issue. Given your history of easy bruising and spontaneous bleeding tendency, have you noticed any mucosal bleeding, such as frequent nosebleeds (epistaxis) or bleeding gums, particularly after dental work?
